discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC by the ATLAS and CMS experiments
motivation: The 2012 observation of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS confirmed the mechanism honoured in 2013, but the experimental achievement itself has never been recognised. Discovering a 125 GeV scalar in a 10^9 Hz collision environment required general-purpose detectors, trigger systems and analysis strategies of unprecedented scale and precision. Peter Jenni (founding ATLAS spokesperson) and Michel Della Negra (founding CMS spokesperson) conceived and led these detectors from the late 1980s through construction. Fabiola Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of discovery and shaped the diphoton and four-lepton strategies that delivered it. Their work opened a new experimental window: direct measurement of Higgs couplings to gauge bosons and fermions, which now tests electroweak symmetry breaking at the percent level. It is a landmark of collaborative experimental physics and merits the Prize.
